Research

Collider physics

ATLAS at the LHC — connecting past and future interests in dark-sector and beyond-Standard-Model searches at high-energy colliders.

Overview

If dark matter interacts with ordinary matter, it might be produced directly in the proton–proton collisions of the Large Hadron Collider. Collider searches probe the same underlying physics as direct detection, but from a complementary direction — and constraints from one inform the interpretation of the other.

The group works on the ATLAS experiment at the LHC, connecting past and ongoing collider searches for dark-sector and beyond-Standard-Model physics to its direct-detection and phenomenology programme.

Current activities

Current activities include relating collider constraints to direct-detection phenomenology, and the development and deployment of AI and machine-learning techniques in analysis.
